claim: Two-zone no-DHW continuation (move_starts) pays 288 SSE per gradient against the fused 97
v1_number: exact reproduction: cont 44 grads, jac 192 sse/grad (96 rows + 96 scalar steps) + cont_fun 4224 (=96/grad); fuse -> 97/grad, cont_fun 0; total SSE 62121 -> 53717; main grads 489 both arms; cont CPU 218 -> 115 ms, capture 1489 -> 1360 ms (-8.7%) at load1 2.86, thread_factor 1.006/1.009
v2_number: horizon-equivalents per optimize(): 51766 prod vs 51722 fused (delta 44 = 0.085%); scalar steps 10464 -> 2016 (-88 scalar horizons), rows 51657 -> 51701 (+44); scalar-step CPU 121 -> 23 ms; solve CPU 2532 -> 2374 ms, prod/fused 1.067 (median of 3 interleaved reps); plan bitwise identical; load1 13.12, thread_factor 1.000
v2_metric: rows of simulate_trajectory_batch + scalar simulate_step calls / n_steps (one row = one full horizon), plus solve thread CPU, via HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize from golden.make, prod vs production _fused_value_and_gradient rewrite, interleaved
null_control: no-continuation arms, same session, interleaved: winter_single_no_dhw and winter_two_zone_dhw -- fuse rewrites 0 calls, every count identical (SSE 2513=2513, 31610=31610; horizons 1658=1658, 30470=30470), plan identical, CPU prod/fused 1.005 and 0.996. Defect/null CPU ratio 1.067/1.00 (V2), 1.094 (V1 capture)
perturbation: --perturb fuse: cont sse/grad 192(+96 fun) -> 97, total SSE 62121 -> 53717; V2 rewrite to jac=True: solve CPU 2532 -> 2374 ms, plan unchanged bitwise
attacks: unit artefact: SSE counts a batch row (a whole 96-step horizon) as 1 but a scalar horizon as 96, so '288 vs 97' and '13.5-31% of total SSE' overstate the work ~100x; in horizons the excess is 98 vs 97 per gradient (+2 scalar horizons, -1 row). The real cost is CPU: the scalar horizons run ~20x a batched row (production comment at _fused_value_and_gradient), giving 6-9% of a two-zone no-DHW solve. Reach: two-zone with DHW off only (DHW scenarios rewrite 0). Fix is value-neutral (bitwise plan).
notes: The 13.5-31.1% grid shares should be restated as CPU shares; the horizon share is 0.085%. Numbers measured at origin/main d749c986d (production byte-identical).

claim: _gil_yield's sleep(0) does not bound loop starvation by an in-process (executor-thread) solve; a 0.1 ms sleep cuts the max gap to ~30 ms
v1_number: gil.py separate invocations, load1 13.1-15.0, thread_factor 1.005-1.030: none winter_two_zone_dhw 83.9 ms / shoulder 65.6 ms (idle 7.0); noyield 25.9 / 13.9 ms (idle 9.9); realsleep 21.4 / 23.6 ms (idle 8.7) -- noyield LOWER than shipped, contradicting 'barely moves'
v2_number: interleaved asyncio heartbeat, winter_two_zone_dhw, median max gap: run A (3 reps, load1 15.77, tf 1.011) idle 13.8, shipped 53.3, noyield 38.8, realsleep 46.9, process 5.6 ms; run B (5 reps, load1 11.30, tf 1.016) idle 6.6, shipped 40.6, noyield 81.3, realsleep 21.1, process 11.5 ms
v2_metric: max/p99 gap of a 1 ms asyncio heartbeat on a real loop with a real ThreadPoolExecutor, all arms interleaved per rep in one process, median over reps
null_control: idle (sleeping job in the pool) 6.6-13.8 ms and the same solve in a spawned worker process (shipped path shape) 5.6-11.5 ms, interleaved with the defect arm. Defect/null ratios: shipped/idle 3.86x and 6.13x, shipped/process 9.48x and 3.52x (asyncio runs only; --hb thread runs rejected, thread_factor 39.4 and 2.0)
perturbation: noyield/shipped max gap 0.73x (A), 2.00x (B); realsleep/shipped 0.88x (A), 0.52x (B); finder claimed noyield ~1x and realsleep 124->29 ms (0.24x). Direction not stable across runs at load1 11-16
attacks: null controls supplied: the in-process starvation itself is real and well separated from both nulls in every run (3.5-9.5x over process). The finding's specific claim -- that the sleep(0) yield is inert and a non-zero sleep fixes it -- rests only on timing and flips between runs (noyield 0.73x vs 2.00x of shipped); a timing-only result is unresolved per the contract. Reach: #511 fallback only; the shipped path runs a worker process, whose arm reads at the null floor.
notes: Needs a quiet-window re-take of the interleaved harness with >=5 reps before any vote either way on the yield. Not the round-8 D9-s1-02 (same id, different finding, refuted in round 8).
